title: Malta Year 8 Math Chapter 1 — Directed Numbers Recap
question: Can you order, add, subtract, multiply and divide directed numbers and use them in word problems?
intro: **Quick recap:** right on the number line is bigger; \(-(-a) = +a\); in \(\times\) and \(\div\), same signs give \(+\) and different signs give \(-\).

questions.title: 1.1 · Biggest number
questions.solution:
\[-20 < -12 < -8 < \boxed{-2}\]

All four are negative, so the one nearest zero wins. \(-20\) looks big because 20 is big, but it is furthest to the left.

questions.title: 1.1 · Greater or smaller
questions.solution:
\[\boxed{-9 < -4}\]

\(-9 > -4\) compares 9 and 4 and forgets the signs; \(9 < -4\) puts a positive below a negative.

questions.title: 1.1 · Ascending order
questions.solution:
\[\boxed{-10,\ -6,\ 0,\ 1,\ 3}\]

B puts \(-6\) before \(-10\) by looking at the sizes only; D is the descending order.

questions.title: 1.2 · Negative + smaller positive
questions.solution:
\[-8 + 3 = -(8 - 3) = \boxed{-5}\]

Answering \(5\) forgets the minus sign — moving 3 right from \(-8\) does not reach zero.

questions.title: 1.2 · Negative + bigger positive
questions.solution:
\[-4 + 11 = 11 - 4 = \boxed{7}\]

\(-7\) has the wrong sign: the positive part is bigger, so the answer is positive. \(-15\) adds the sizes.

questions.title: 1.2 · Spending more than you have
questions.prompt: You have €9 and spend €15. Work out \(9 - 15\).
questions.solution:
\[9 - 15 = -(15 - 9) = \boxed{-6}\]

You are €6 short. Writing \(6\) loses the sign.

questions.title: 1.2 · Missing number
questions.solution:
From \(-6\) to \(-13\) is 7 steps left:

\[-6 + (\boxed{-7}) = -13\]

\(7\) goes the wrong way: \(-6 + 7 = 1\).

questions.title: 1.2 · Subtracting a negative
questions.solution:
\[5 - (-4) = 5 + 4 = \boxed{9}\]

\(1\) ignores the second minus sign: two minus signs side by side make a plus.

questions.title: 1.3 · Two negatives multiplied
questions.solution:
Same signs give a positive:

\[(-6)\times(-7) = \boxed{42}\]

\(-42\) is the answer for different signs.

questions.title: 1.3 · Negative divided by positive
questions.solution:
Different signs give a negative:

\[(-36)\div4 = \boxed{-9}\]

\(9\) drops the sign.

questions.title: 1.3 · Which answer is negative?
questions.solution:
\[(-2)\times6 = \boxed{-12}\]

A and B have two minus signs, so they are positive (\(15\) and \(5\)).

questions.title: 1.4 · Freezer temperature
questions.prompt: A freezer is at \(-15\,^\circ\text{C}\). It warms up by \(9\,^\circ\text{C}\). What is the new temperature, in °C?
questions.solution:
\[-15 + 9 = \boxed{-6\,^\circ\text{C}}\]

\(-24\) makes it colder; warming up moves right on the number line.

questions.title: 1.4 · Lift floors
questions.prompt: A lift goes from level \(-2\) (a basement) up to level \(5\). How many floors does it go up?
questions.solution:
\[5 - (-2) = 5 + 2 = \boxed{7}\]

Count them: \(-2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5\) — 7 moves. \(3\) forgets the floors below ground.

takeaway: Right on the number line is bigger; adding a positive moves right and taking away moves left; two minus signs side by side make a plus; and in × and ÷, same signs give + while different signs give −.
